title: MongoDB Indexes
summary: Create lookup indexes and enforce unique values in the database.

richText: An index stores selected field values in a form MongoDB can search without scanning every document.
Indexes can improve reads but require storage and extra work when documents change.
A unique index rejects duplicate indexed values. An application lookup before saving cannot enforce uniqueness under concurrent writes.
Existing duplicate values can prevent creation of a unique index.
@Indexed describes an index on a mapped field. The annotation alone does not prove the database index exists.
Automatic index creation is disabled by default in Spring Data MongoDB.
Create required indexes deliberately, either through deployment migrations or explicit application setup.
Check the actual database indexes when diagnosing duplicate-value behavior.

example.title: Create a unique username index
description: This setup assumes a mapped User document with a userName field.
Run this inside controlled database setup code with an injected MongoTemplate named mongoTemplate.
The collection must not contain duplicate usernames before this index is created.
explanation: The index applies to the collection mapped by User.
unique rejects duplicate userName values after the index exists.
